learning: If slalom line-loss falls further with the oval holding, kd is still a lever and the final race can use this value. If s-bend or the oval drops, kd has passed its useful range, and 0.6 is the final choice. Flat slalom line-loss would point to line_loss mode as the remaining controller lever.
notes: Geometry held at the iteration 9 best values. Controller changed only in kd (0.6 to 0.75) to continue the measured trend in which kd raised from 0.45 to 0.6 cut slalom line-loss from 1.9 to 1.1 with the oval flat. Revert kd to 0.6 if the oval oscillates above about 0.35 or falls below 16/20.
rationale: The Builder holds the iteration 9 geometry (wheel_track 0.09 m, span ±0.03 m at 0.015 m spacing, y 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.5 kg). I keep it exactly. Only the controller changes. Evidence from the controller-only steps on this geometry: iteration 7 (kp 2.5, kd 0.3) scored 400.0; iteration 8 (kp 3.0, kd 0.45) scored 610.7 with s-bend 15/20 and oval 20/20; iteration 9 (kd 0.6) scored 669.8 with s-bend 20/20, oval 20/20 and slalom line-loss down from 1.9 to 1.1. Oval steering_oscillation was essentially flat across those steps (0.216, then 0.219), so the jitter guard has room. The slalom line-loss trend is still falling with kd, while kp 3.0 is retained. I therefore step kd from 0.6 to 0.75 and keep kp 3.0, ki 0, base_speed 1.2, the sensor weights and last_direction, so the change is attributable to kd alone. Expected result (not measured): oval and s-bend hold at 20/20 and 19 to 20/20, with slalom line-loss below 1.1 per run. Guard: if oval steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35 or the oval falls below 16/20, return kd to 0.6, the best measured value. The final unseen track is not known, so this is a modest step, not a tuned-to-slalom step.
